ANSWER: All of it is in `src/http/mod.rs`.

- **`origin_allowed(origin: &str, shared: &Shared) -> bool`** (`src/http/mod.rs:334`) makes the decision. It trims any trailing `/` from the Origin and lowercases it. It then accepts the origin if any one of these holds:
  1. It matches an entry in `shared.allow_origins`, or that list contains `*`.
  2. It equals the server's own origin, which `origin_of(&shared.base_url)` (`src/http/mod.rs:112`) builds as `scheme://host[:port]`, lowercased.
  3. It comes from the local machine: `host_of(&o).is_some_and(|h| is_loopback_host(&h))`.
- **`is_loopback_host(host: &str) -> bool`** (`src/http/mod.rs:96`) is the local-machine check. It strips `[`/`]` from IPv6 addresses and returns true for `localhost` or for any IP address that parses as loopback (`IpAddr::is_loopback()`, so 127.x.x.x and ::1).
- **`host_of(url: &str)`** (`src/http/mod.rs:102`) is a helper that takes the host out of `scheme://host[:port]/...` and drops the port, so it can be passed to `is_loopback_host`.

The request handler calls `origin_allowed` twice. At line 380 it rejects a request whose Origin is not allowed. At line 393 it sends CORS headers back only when the Origin is allowed. `is_loopback_host` is also used at line 214, when the server checks whether a plain `http://` base URL points at the local machine.

CONFIDENCE: high
